subject: Invoice recipient chain and tax documentation for cloud marketplace co-sell
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: CloudCorp Procurement <procure@cloudcorp.com>, marketplace-billing@azure.microsoft.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice recipient chain and tax documentation for cloud marketplace co-sell

Hi team,

Quick one — CloudCorp flagged that the Azure marketplace invoice we received (invoice AZ-1234) was issued to our US entity (Redwood Inference, Inc.) but CloudCorp needs settlement invoiced to their EU entity (CloudCorp Ltd, VAT: GB999999999). They also asked for explicit VAT reverse-charge evidence tied to the marketplace transaction and a reissued invoice or credit memo that shows the EU entity as the recipient.

Questions:
- Does Azure marketplace support reissuing an invoice to a different buyer entity post-transaction, or do we need to route a settlement credit/offset through our co-sell reseller mapping?
- What documentation will satisfy the CloudCorp procurement/VAT team for reverse-charge (VAT registration number + signed purchasing statement, or do they require the marketplace provider to stamp proof)?
- If we need to provide tax evidence, I attached the marketplace invoice and CloudCorp's VAT cert. Can Finance prepare a draft credit + reissue playbook or language we can send to the marketplace billing team?

Attachments: sample_marketplace_invoice_AZ-1234.pdf, cloudcorp_vat_certificate.pdf

Next steps I propose: Kimberly take point with Azure billing; Jordan to confirm settlement mapping on the co-sell SKU; Vivek to confirm whether listing metadata supports alternate invoicing entity for co-sell deals.

Thanks,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.com
From: CloudCorp Procurement <procure@cloudcorp.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 13:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Invoice recipient chain and tax documentation for cloud marketplace co-sell

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the quick note and the attachments. To confirm our side:
- CloudCorp Ltd (GB) must be listed as the invoice recipient for VAT accounting purposes.
- We can accept a credit memo from Redwood plus a freshly issued invoice from Azure showing CloudCorp Ltd as buyer; alternatively the marketplace bill can remain to Redwood if Redwood issues a settlement invoice to CloudCorp Ltd showing the exact amount charged by Azure and referencing invoice AZ-1234.
- For reverse-charge, we require CloudCorp's VAT registration (attached) and a short statement confirming the purchase is for business-to-business services and that CloudCorp is the recipient for VAT purposes. If Azure can provide a marketplace transaction proof with their buyer field set to CloudCorp Ltd, that is preferred.

If Redwood can prepare a settlement invoice referencing AZ-1234 and sign a seller declaration, we can accept that and process payment to Redwood's EU entity bank account.

Regards,
Maya Singh
Senior Procurement Manager
CloudCorp
procure@cloudcorp.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, CloudCorp Procurement <procure@cloudcorp.com>, marketplace-billing@azure.microsoft.com
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice recipient chain and tax documentation for cloud marketplace co-sell

Thanks — looping Finance in with the specifics. Quick realities from our side (Azure experience):
- Azure billing APIs do not typically reissue invoices to a different legal buyer after the billing run; marketplace provider may issue a credit and then generate a corrected invoice, but that is done on a case-by-case basis and often requires marketplace support tickets and partner onboarding checks.
- Practically, the fastest path is Redwood issues an internal settlement invoice (EU legal entity) to CloudCorp that references the Azure invoice number and provides a statement for VAT reverse-charge. That invoice will be our seller-side document for CloudCorp to account for VAT.
- We'll need to gather: Redwood EU entity VAT details, banking details for CloudCorp payout (if different), signed W-9/W-8 as relevant for withholding, and a short seller declaration.

I've started a draft settlement invoice template and attached a placeholder W-9 for Redwood (w9_redwood_signed.pdf) so CloudCorp can confirm whether they still prefer market provider reissue.

Action items:
- Grace: confirm Redwood EU entity VAT + bank account info (if we will bill them from EU).
- Jordan: confirm which co-sell SKU/offer id maps to the marketplace invoice so we can reference it exactly.
- Vivek: can you check listing metadata and whether reseller pass-through or buyer override flags exist on the listing?

Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice recipient chain and tax documentation for cloud marketplace co-sell

On Tue, Aug 10, 2027 at 10:03 AM Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com> wrote:

Hi all,

Adding the co-sell mapping details: the SKU on AZ invoice AZ-1234 maps to offer_id: redwood-llm-prod-01. In our co-sell settlement flow we can generate seller-side invoices that mirror marketplace billing — provided we include the marketplace invoice reference and make clear the settlement is for the Azure charge.

Important note: if the marketplace requires funds to flow via the marketplace escrow for revenue recognition, we need to confirm whether Azure will accept a seller-generated invoice at their billing reconciliation stage. If not, the credit/offset path (Azure issues credit; Azure reissues) is the clean accounting route but slower.

I recommend we present CloudCorp with two options and a timeline: (A) Redwood issues EU settlement invoice with reverse-charge statement (fast, ~3-5 business days to prep + make bookkeeping entry) or (B) request Azure reissue — likely 2-4 weeks depending on marketplace support.

Jordan Blake
Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Thanks — did a quick check of the listing metadata and notes from Marketplace enablement: the offer supports resale mapping but there is no automatic buyer-entity override after settlement. We can:

- Toggle a reseller pass-through flag for future orders (prevents buyer misalignment going forward).
- For this transaction we should proceed with Kimberly's settlement invoice approach (Redwood EU invoice referencing AZ-1234) and include CloudCorp's VAT number and a succinct statement for reverse-charge.

I'll draft the exact text for the seller declaration and add a HubSpot note to deal HC-4582. Also attaching a DocuSign template we can use for CloudCorp to sign acknowledgment (link below).
